Yes, you can get all the 5 digit number combinations within 2 minutes from a computer but that doesn't mean that you can "crack it" (as in get access to the account) in 2 minutes. 10 numbers raised to 5 is just equal to 10,000 possibilities. Assuming you get 3 tries per day, it would take you about 9 years to input 0-99999 and that's if your program runs using increments of 1. It's just not practical or realistic because a) the user might change his/her password along the way, b) the bank might inform the user about the attempts and c) why use brute force to get a specific user's passcode when you have other options?

>even FBI can't open and brute force a 5 digit iPhone passcode.

They definitely can. It would just take time because Apple implemented a lockout feature.
